title: Notebook cell source array: value split between list elements
summary: A synthetic notebook whose one code cell assigns an AWS-secret-access-key-shaped value to a variable named aws_secret_access_key. In one projection the cell source is a list with one element per line and the value is inside a single element; in the second the same value is divided between two adjacent source elements, so no single JSON string in the file holds it.
rationale: The notebook format stores multi-line strings either as one string or as a list of strings that is joined with an empty string. The raw bytes of a split value are separated by a closing quote, a comma, a line break and an opening quote, which belong to the JSON array and not to the value. Failure mode: covering only the first fragment, or treating the quote-and-comma gap as part of the secret. This is a format-level rebuild rule stated by the format owner, a different mechanism from language string concatenation or a shell line continuation. The split position inside the value is an authored stress variant derived from the permission to split a list; it is not an observed notebook, and the specification does not say where a producer splits. Preconditions: the reading that holds the intact value requires parsing the JSON and joining the elements, so whether a consumer does that is a downstream, unmeasured capability (credential-eval handoff #150), not an assumption here.

expectation.rationale: Flag the whole value in both projections; in the split projection cover each fragment (the two array elements) and give the quote, comma and line break between them no secret role. Two statements are combined by a step a reviewer can repeat: the notebook format states that a multi-line string field written as a list of strings is joined with an empty string when read back and that readers must accept a string or a list of strings; and the IAM user guide states that the secret access key can be retrieved only at creation and must not be given to unauthorized parties, with the variable name aws_secret_access_key on the value's own line as the documented key-name context of the family contract. Synthetic and never issued: each value was built from an authored stem (SYNTHETIC plus a role word plus NEVERISSUED), zero padding and a fixed tail so that it matches the 40-character shape but is not a value any AWS account issued; no notebook was executed, so every output block is authored text, not a recording.

sources.supports: When these fields are written to disk, they may be written as a list of strings, which should be joined with '' when reading back into memory; if you work with notebook files directly, you must allow multi-line string fields to be either a string or list of strings.
The same sentence about lists of strings joined with '' appears in the 5.2.0 page; no change between the two versions was found for this statement.
misc.multiline_string is oneOf a string or an array of strings, and cell source is "Contents of the cell, represented as an array of lines" using it.
access key = ID + secret used together; secret retrievable only at creation; do not provide access keys to unauthorized parties
